analysis:
Both changed files are offline CI test scripts, .github/scripts/test-threat-bedrock.py and .github/scripts/test-threat-budget.py. They change no provider, coordinator, attestation, key, cache or fan-helper code, so no canonical asset or boundary is affected. T-041 and the TB-0xx entries describe provider and native runtime behavior, and none of them is touched.

The new tests encode fail-closed behavior in the review tooling:
- A report without manual_review_reasons cannot clear a merge (bedrock test lines 283-285).
- A human-review-required result is not clean (lines 267-272).
- Malformed cache entries and invalid JSON responses stop without spending or leaking response text (budget test).
- Bedrock error diagnostics record only the SDK error code and RequestId, never provider messages or source (bedrock test lines 191-217).
- A fallback failure keeps the correct backup call identity (lines 219-226).
- Citation permission is not widened by head-only excerpt orientation (budget test, head-only excerpt case).

The production implementations (threat_review.merge_policy, bedrock, budget_scan) were not supplied. Their correctness is therefore unverified; this is a coverage limit, not evidence of safety. No new attack surface or threat-model gap was found in the supplied diff.
